answer.text: A bank authorized under FEMA to undertake all current and capital account transactions as directed by RBI
Any commercial bank registered with SEBI
A bank with assets over Rs. 10,000 crore
A bank that is a member of a stock exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: An AD Category-I Bank is a scheduled commercial, state, or urban cooperative bank authorized under Section 10(1) of FEMA to undertake all current and capital account transactions according to RBI directions. The Trap: The AD licence is issued under FEMA (not SEBI) and specifically covers foreign exchange transactions, not general bank registration. Note: AD Category-I banks may become trading and clearing members of currency derivative exchanges on their own account and on client account, subject to prudential requirements and NOPL.
